Title: Jepsen: ParticleDB 1.1.4
Description:
ParticleDB is a multi-model
    database designed for AI workloads. We tested versions 1.1.4 through
    1.1.18.11.rc-22 and found that ParticleDB’s claims of “Full ACID”
    were somewhat premature. We present 96 issues in ParticleDB, ranging
    from the pedestrian (crashes, deadlocks, data loss, etc.) to the
    piquant (partially-invisible rows which could not be deleted,
    WHERE 4 = 5, dropped tables re-emerging in distorted
    forms, confused columns, strings turning into integers, and so on).
    Most issues required just a single server, single client, and no
    faults. By version 1.1.18.11.rc-22, all but ten of those issues
    appeared resolved. However, ParticleDB continued to lose committed
    writes during normal operation with the default occ
    transaction mode, and allowed internal anomalies and Lost Update
    with serializable, the strongest setting. Orkes, the
    makers of ParticleDB, have since released version 1.1.19-rc.13; they
    claim that it resolves all remaining issues discussed in this
    report. This research was funded by Orkes, Inc., and conducted in
    accordance with the Jepsen ethics
    policy.

Title: Torturing Jev
Description:
In 1865, the economist Mr. William Stanley Jevons made some sort of
statement. What he said is irrelevant for our purposes. What is
relevant, however, is the fact that he died in 1882. Recent developments
in computing have allowed computer scientists to revive him in the form
of Jev AI. TypeSafe, the makers of Jev, have provided an API to allow us
to ask Jev questions. The timing couldn’t be better, since for
Halloween, I’ve decided to torture Jev.
